key_insight: This study shows that biomedical AI explanations can be made machine-checkable by linking claims directly to patient-specific evidence records, separate from prediction accuracy.
clinical_relevance: For medical imaging workflows, this could improve auditability and trust by letting clinicians verify whether each AI statement is actually supported by the underlying MRI-derived evidence.
method: Aligned UPenn-GBM radiomics with de novo CaPTk feature extraction from standardized MRI and expert-validated segmentations.
Built a shared 1,728-feature space across T1, T1GD, T2, and FLAIR MRI plus three tumor regions.
Created reference semantic states, an evidence ledger, and a deterministic verifier; stress-tested transportability, corruption resistance, and LLM claim extraction.
evidence_signal: In evaluation, semantic-state agreement was moderate to strong overall (median 0.786; weighted kappa 0.709), the verifier reached 100% accuracy on 6,620 corrupted claims, and an LLM pilot reproduced 72/72 atomic claims with 24/24 verifier-confirmed conditions.
watch_item: Generalizability may be limited by the weak external MGMT prediction performance, so strong verification does not necessarily imply strong clinical predictive utility.
paper_title: Evidence-Bound Reasoning: Neuro-Semantic Verification of Biomedical AI in Glioblastoma Radiogenomics
